clue.text: Careless to omit heading from postulate

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter, and omitting it drops that letter

blocks.note: a premiss (a variant spelling of premise) is a proposition postulated in an argument

explanation.surface: Someone sloppily forgets to put the title on a proposition they are putting forward.
explanation.walkthrough: PREMISS is the older British spelling of premise; losing its P leaves REMISS.
explanation.definitionFit: Remiss is a synonym for negligent, lax in attending to one's duty.

clue.text: Censure for blocking a stretch of river

indicators.note: a word blocking a stretch sits in the middle of it

blocks.note: a reach is a straight length of river
pro is Latin for for, as in pros and cons

explanation.surface: Criticism of obstructing part of a waterway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For' looks like a link word but is Latin pro, as in pros and cons.
explanation.definitionFit: To reproach is to express disapproval or blame, a close synonym of censure.

clue.text: Game to hold army function in a month

indicators.note: one word holding others keeps them within its arms

blocks.note: the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve
a do is a party or social function

explanation.surface: A sporting fixture is arranged to host a military event some time in one month.
explanation.walkthrough: Matador is a card game and also a version of dominoes, not only the bullfighter. TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Matador is the name of a card game and a dominoes variant, a lesser-known sense beyond bullfighting.

clue.text: Creature bound to approach reserve half-heartedly

indicators.note: with half its heart gone, one of the two central letters of the word is lost

blocks.note: a bound is a spring or leap

explanation.surface: An animal leaps towards a nature reserve without much enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: BOOK's heart is OO; losing half of it leaves BOK. 'Reserve' looks like a noun for a game park, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The springbok is a southern African gazelle, an animal known for leaping.

clue.text: French art is housed by officer retreating into fantasy

indicators.note: something housed by another thing sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: taken as written, placed inside CAPT

explanation.surface: French painting kept in an army officer's home, the officer daydreaming away from reality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Art' is the archaic verb (thou art), not painting: French 'tu es'.
explanation.definitionFit: An escapist habitually seeks distraction from reality, so as an adjective it describes someone withdrawing into daydreams.

clue.text: Usual times, only changing concurrently

indicators.note: changing the words alters them, so their letters take a new order

explanation.surface: Routine timetables are only being altered at the same moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Simultaneously means at the same time, which is what concurrently also expresses.

clue.text: A type of grain or fruit

explanation.surface: A question of classifying produce as cereal or fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: The acorn is the nut of the oak, which botanists count as a fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: An acorn is the nut of the oak tree, botanically a fruit containing its seed.

clue.text: Brutal husband meets university graduate in pub

indicators.note: the people meeting are placed inside the drinking place

explanation.surface: A violent spouse runs into a college graduate in a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Meets' is only joining the pieces; the husband, university and graduate all go together inside the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Inhuman means cruel and lacking compassion, so it is a synonym of brutal.

clue.text: Some deputy ran this for Nero, perhaps

indicators.note: some of the following words means only part of their letters are used

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of deputy, all of ran and the start of this

explanation.surface: An underling administered this on behalf of the Roman emperor.
explanation.definitionFit: Nero was a notoriously cruel Roman emperor, an example of a despotic ruler.

clue.text: Complaint over image leads to anxiety about new course

indicators.note: one word about another surrounds it

blocks.note: a chill is a minor illness, and complaint means an ailment

explanation.surface: A grievance about a picture leads to worry about a new class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complaint' is an ailment, not a grievance, and 'over' in a down clue means placed above. 'Course' is a dish in a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Chilli con carne is a spicy minced beef and bean dish served as a course of a meal.

clue.text: Safe artificial material for stiffening

blocks.note: peter is old criminal slang for a safe

explanation.surface: A description of some synthetic fabric that can be relied on to stiffen garments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Safe' looks like an adjective; it is the noun, a strongbox, which crooks called a peter.
explanation.definitionFit: Petersham is a stiff corded ribbon used to reinforce waistbands and hat bands.

clue.text: Additional reading matter given by ambassador to king

blocks.note: the Old Testament, read aloud in church
His Excellency, the title of an ambassador
R for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: An extra book is handed by a diplomat to a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: An ambassador is addressed as His Excellency, abbreviated HE.
explanation.definitionFit: Other can mean further or extra, as in 'one other thing', matching additional.

clue.text: Possibly first book used in the service

blocks.note: first meaning: a number giving position in a sequence, of which first is one example
second meaning: a book setting out the forms of a church rite, especially ordination

explanation.surface: Perhaps the first book a congregation uses during worship.
explanation.definitionFit: First, second and third are ordinal numbers; an ordinal is also the clergy's service book for ordaining priests.

clue.text: Platelayer's mother is cutting hard-wearing fabric

indicators.note: a word cutting another slices into it, so it sits within the other word

blocks.note: linen is a strong, durable cloth

explanation.surface: A railway worker's mum is busy cutting some tough cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay. MA goes inside LINEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A lineman maintains railway track, and a platelayer is the British term for a worker laying and repairing rails.

clue.text: Tree died, grazed by vehicle

blocks.note: a car is a road vehicle
abbreviation of Latin obiit, he or she died, seen on gravestones

explanation.surface: A tree is killed after a car scrapes against it.
explanation.walkthrough: The died abbreviation comes from Latin obiit, seen on gravestones; 'grazed by' puts the vehicle first.
explanation.definitionFit: The carob is a Mediterranean evergreen whose pods are used as a chocolate substitute.

clue.text: Country, people given short answer by island queen

blocks.note: a rani is an Indian queen

explanation.surface: Rural folk are curtly replied to by a monarch reigning over an island.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as 'a country's people'. 'Country' looks like it gives IRAN on its own, but the wordplay is I plus RANI followed by ANS.
explanation.definitionFit: Iranians are the citizens of one Middle Eastern nation, so they are that country's people.

clue.text: Dine out with Siamese money just the same

indicators.note: out can mean disordered or put out of place, so the letters move

blocks.note: the tical was the old currency of Siam, now Thailand

explanation.surface: Eating out using Thai cash costs exactly what it would anywhere else.
explanation.walkthrough: Siamese twins are identical, an echo of the surface; but 'Siamese money' is the tical, Thailand's former coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Identical means exactly alike in every respect, the same.

clue.text: Laws of nations broken by unionist extremists

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two end letters, the only ones kept
a word broken by another is split open with the other placed within

blocks.note: the first and last letters of unionist

explanation.surface: A country's legislation is defied by hardline union members.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unionist extremists' reads as hardliners, but it means just the ends of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Statutes are written laws passed by a legislative body.

clue.text: Moral fibre of bishop in retreat as an individual

indicators.note: something put in goes between the other pieces, so the churchman sits within the rest

blocks.note: to back off is to retreat

explanation.surface: A churchman shows strong character by withdrawing alone into seclusion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' places the bishop between the two other pieces rather than inside a single word.
explanation.definitionFit: Backbone figuratively means strength of character or resolve, which is what moral fibre denotes.

clue.text: A conspirator runs further up the tree

blocks.note: an instruction, not letters: the runs letter is moved higher in this down entry
Brutus conspired against Julius Caesar; his R is the one moved

explanation.surface: A plotter flees higher up a tree to escape.
explanation.walkthrough: Brutus, the conspirator against Caesar, is written after A, then his R moves one place further up this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The arbutus, or strawberry tree, is an evergreen tree with red berries.

clue.text: Half of them paid a worker from the country

indicators.note: half of a four-letter word keeps two of its letters, here the back pair

blocks.note: the second half of the word them
to meet a bill is to pay it, so met means paid

explanation.surface: Some of the group settled the wages of a farmhand.
explanation.walkthrough: A worker is an ant, and emmet is the old dialect word for an ant, used in rural speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Emmet is a rural dialect word for the ant, the classic worker insect.

clue.text: Wealthy male with the same forefather

definitions.note: an adjective standing for a noun: a wealthy person

blocks.note: agnate means descended from a common male ancestor

explanation.surface: A rich man shares an ancestor with someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnate is a rich and powerful business figure, so the word stands for a wealthy person.

clue.text: Coral, for example, is above the ground

explanation.surface: Coral grows higher than the seabed.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'above' simply means the first piece comes before the second. A coral island is an atoll.
explanation.definitionFit: Coral reefs and atolls form islands in the sea, so a coral is one type of island.

clue.text: Dull coach rebuffed by footballers around America

indicators.note: something rebuffed is sent back the way it came, so the word runs backwards
one piece wrapped around another holds it inside

blocks.note: a coach is a long-distance bus

explanation.surface: A boring coach trip is snubbed by football players around the States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dull' is the definition, not a description of the coach. Subfusc is also the dark formal dress worn at Oxford exams.
explanation.definitionFit: Subfusc means dark or drab in colour, sombre and lacking brightness.

clue.text: Relative, about fifty, embraced by a Parisienne

indicators.note: something embraced is held within arms, so it goes inside

blocks.note: une is the French feminine for a
c is short for circa, Latin for about
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A kinsman of around fifty is hugged by a Frenchwoman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About fifty' reads as an age; it is C plus L going inside UNE.
explanation.definitionFit: An uncle is a parent's brother, a family relative.

clue.text: Mean to follow on horseback, though tense and nervy

blocks.note: a jockey who is riding is said to be up

explanation.surface: A stingy person rides behind, anxious all the while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On horseback' means riding, as in 'jockey up'; 'to follow' puts the stingy word after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Uptight is an informal word for anxious and edgy, unable to relax.

clue.text: Classically elegant screen with both ends missing

indicators.note: losing both ends removes the first and final letters of the word

blocks.note: a lattice is a criss-cross screen of strips

explanation.surface: A refined, classical screen whose edges have been lopped off.
explanation.walkthrough: LATTICE without its L and E leaves ATTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Attic describes the pure, simple style of ancient Athens, so it means refined in the classical manner.

clue.text: Unwilling to let cat run wild

indicators.note: running wild means moving without any order, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written; the word also helps indicate the shuffle

explanation.surface: Someone is loath to allow their pet cat to roam free.
explanation.definitionFit: Reluctant means disinclined or hesitant to do something.

clue.text: Divide society into diverse parts

indicators.note: putting one thing into another places it inside
used as a verb, parts means separates and splits up, so these letters are broken apart and reordered

explanation.surface: Split a community into varied sections.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diverse parts' reads as one phrase, but 'parts' is a verb shuffling DIVERSE, with S slipped in.
explanation.definitionFit: To dissever is to separate or sever into pieces, a formal synonym of divide.

clue.text: Tool for building jetties across lake

indicators.note: something lying across another spans it, so the outer word wraps around

explanation.surface: An implement used for constructing landing stages across a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For building' reads as part of the definition, but 'building' joins 'jetties' as the outer word.
explanation.definitionFit: Pliers are a hand tool with pincer jaws for gripping and bending.
